sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (bijural federal state; Quebec civil law not applicable to BC corporations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2007 Protocol)
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2012, in force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Pt II.1 and Pt XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky Law); FINTRAC guidance on PEP and sanctions screening. The federal CBCA public register of individuals with significant control (Corporations Canada, in force 22 January 2024) does NOT apply to a company incorporated under the BC Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c 57); the BC Land Owner Transparency Act applies only if the SPV acquires land, which is outside the current mandate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public Office in the UBO's country of residence (e.g., PRC Notary Public Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized provincial foreign affairs office (Convention in force for PRC since 07 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence / business license and constitutional documents of the direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., PRC State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille at the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the ultimate parent authorizing incorporation of the BC ULC, appointment of officers, and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent company (certified by corporate secretary and notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille applied to the notarized resolution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and certificate of incumbency for the direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the parent's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or direct banker's verification under FINTRAC verification rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing of the direct corporate shareholder (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the direct shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners (25% or greater) against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act), Global Affairs Canada sanctions, and the OFAC SDN list as applied by Canadian financial institutions; enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including verification of source of wealth and source of funds; mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting to FINTRAC under PCMLTFA ss 7 and 7.1; engagement categorized as Medium-Risk Enhanced for AML purposes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services (Corporate Online) / onebc.ca; Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must consist of a distinctive element plus a descriptive element and the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' (French forms 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' or 'S.R.I.') under s 25 of the BC Business Corporations Act and the Business Corporations Regulation; names must be expressible in Roman script in English or French form; transliterated names in pinyin or other Romanized forms are accepted, whereas names rendered exclusively in non-Latin script are not; the name must not be confusingly similar to an existing corporate name or trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Insurance, Credit Union, Loan and related financial tokens (licensing or consent of financial regulator required)
Engineer / Engineering (Engineers and Geoscientists BC certificate required)
Royal, Crown, Government, Canada, British Columbia (ministerial authorization required)
Olympic, Red Cross, Nobel (protected treaty or enacted marks)
Terms implying connection with a government, crown agency, or political party
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name approval is reserved for 56 days and may be renewed online before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a revised Name Request with a fresh NUANS report; (2) request reconsideration by the Senior Name Approval Officer; and (3) where the refusal is legally contestable, proceed to judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act. Trademark conflicts must be cleared by counsel before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a passive equity-holding SPV provided the registered office is a physical street address in British Columbia at which records are kept and process may be served during business hours; a post-office box alone is prohibited. Corporate service provider offices are widely used and accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5% annually) for a pure equity-holding SPV with no premises or employees; the Registrar may require production of records on complaint or under BCBCA investigation powers, and the registered-agent facility serves as the company's stated address for service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and NUANS name search report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (Ministry of Finance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of articles, notice of articles, consents, and UBO/transparency register setup
Notarization, certified translation, and Hague Apostille of UBO and parent corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CAD 300-600 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: FINTRAC-compliant KYC file assembly, PEP identification, and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance advisor / BC law firm

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10-15 (incorporation), ss. 36-44 (shares), ss. 45-53 (registered office and records office), ss. 109-129 (directors and officers); Business Corporations Act Regulation, B.C. Reg. 358/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Government of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) together with Notice of Articles (Form 2) and Articles
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or contribution deposit requirement. Shares may be issued for any lawful consideration authorized by the Articles. Because this is an Unlimited Liability Company, shareholder liability is unlimited and the legal name must include 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscriptions of the founding shareholders set out in the register are accepted, and the corresponding common shares are issued as fully paid for the consideration stated in the books. (2) The registered office of the Company is fixed at [address in British Columbia], and the records office is established at the same address. (3) The persons named in the Notice of Articles are confirmed as first directors to hold office until the next annual general meeting. (4) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each with authority, acting singly, to execute filings, open bank accounts, and sign routine contracts. (5) The officers are directed to complete all BC registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online), Ministry of Citizens' Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into BC Registries Corporate Online and run the mandatory name search. Provide proposed name ending with 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. Submit a name reservation request with up to three alternatives and pay the prescribed name reservation fee. The system checks against existing BC and federal corporate names and marks confusing names for refusal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, immediately file a revised Name Reservation Request with alternate names; a rejected name may be reconsidered only if the conflict is resolved by consent letter or registrar's ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries / Company filer or authorized legal professional via Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Incorporation Application), Form 2 (Notice of Articles), and Articles. The Articles must authorize the class of shares to be issued, name the first directors, and specify the registered and records office addresses in British Columbia. Include the ULC legal element exactly as reserved. Execute Consents to Act as Director for each initial director. Digital authentication is sufficient; notarization is not required.
required_dossiers: Executed consents of the first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry flags omissions, correct the relevant form within the prescribed response window and resubmit through Corporate Online; if the share authority is defective, file corrected articles or a special resolution amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Filing and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the prepared package through Corporate Online, pay the official filing fee of C$350 (approximately US$258) using the registry payment gateway, and submit. The Registrar examines the application, registers the company, assigns a BC company number, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon successful review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, review the deficiency notice, amend the affected form, and resubmit within the registry's stated deadline; a fresh filing and fee are required only if the original application is cancelled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Company Summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, and the Company Summary from Corporate Online or request certified copies. Verify the legal name, company number, ULC designation, incorporation date, registered office, and first directors. Retain these documents for banking and tax filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any detail in the certificate or company summary is inaccurate, submit a correction application supported by the original filed documents and pay only the prescribed correction fee, if any.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Registered Office, Records Office, and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution confirming the registered office and records office address in British Columbia. Open the statutory registers (members, directors, officers, share issuances) and maintain them at the records office. Obtain the landlord's or service provider's consent to use the address as registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the intended address becomes unavailable, hold an extraordinary board resolution and file the appropriate notice of change of registered office/records office with BC Registries; the new office must be an approved physical address in BC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Officers and Complete Institutional Banking KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; financial institution/Anti-Money Laundering compliance unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the first board meeting, appoint the President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer by resolution. Execute certificate of incumbency, bank account opening resolution, and signatory specimens. Submit corporate documents and beneficial ownership information to the bank. As the SPV is a passive holding vehicle, complete enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and ultimate controller declarations.
required_dossiers: Ultimate beneficial ownership/source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution requests additional KYC information, provide the corporate ownership chart, declaration of UBOs, and transaction purpose letter; if the account application is declined, modify the ownership or control structure or apply to a different regulated financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax and Business Numbers (CRA and BC Tax Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance (single-window through CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC for a federal Business Number (BN) and corporate income tax account using CRA's Business Registration Online. Activate GST/HST, payroll, or import/export accounts only if a taxable activity, employees, or trade actually exist. For BC, corporate income tax is administered by CRA, so no separate provincial corporate tax registration is required. File T2 corporate income tax returns annually even if the SPV has no income.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA account is not activated due to identity mismatch, update the BC company records and provide Form RC245 or supporting declaration; then re-submit through Business Registration Online or call CRA business enquiries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Industrial/Environmental Licensing Exemption and Local Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing and building departments; WorkSafeBC only if employees are later added
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that passive equity holding (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112) is outside BC's provincial industrial licensing and environmental assessment triggers. If a physical office is maintained, determine whether a municipal business licence and zoning/occupancy permit are required (e.g., Vancouver Business Licence). Arrange fire safety inspection under the BC Fire Code and obtain occupancy clearance. No environmental impact assessment is triggered. Re-evaluate these duties if operations expand beyond passive holding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality imposes a licence requirement, apply through its online portal and demonstrate passive management use; if refused on zoning grounds, request a variance or appeal to the applicable board of variance with a written land-use rationale.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no provincial industrial licensing board assumes jurisdiction over a passive equity-holding SPV (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112); municipal authorities may regulate the physical office, if any.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating, manufacturing, or sectoral permit is required for holding subsidiary shares and receiving dividends.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy / Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not applicable — no physical undertaking, construction, or industrial activity triggers an EIA under the Environmental Assessment Act or the Environmental Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or waste discharge limits attach to a pure equity-holding SPV. Any administrative office must comply with municipal wastewater and solid-waste bylaws; no measurable emissions are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a passive SPV without employees, no civil-defence or workplace clearance is mandatory. If an office is occupied, obtain an occupancy permit and fire safety clearance from the authority having jurisdiction under the BC Fire Code; if employees are later engaged, register with WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is the national tax administrator for federal income tax and GST/HST; the British Columbia Ministry of Finance / BC Tax Services Branch administers BC provincial corporate income tax and the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST). Corporate registration is effected through the BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online / BC OneStop. Principal portals are CRA My Business Account, CRA GST/HST NETFILE, BC eTaxBC, and the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate or continue the ULC under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act; British Columbia permits unlimited liability companies, imposes no minimum capital requirement, and allows non-resident ownership. Step 2: Obtain BC corporate registry documentation from the BC Registrar of Companies. Step 3: Register the ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or through My Business Account; CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number with program account suffixes, including RC0001 for GST/HST, RM0001 for import/export reporting, and RP0001 for payroll. Step 4: Register through BC eTaxBC for PST if the ULC intends to make taxable sales of goods or services in British Columbia; PST registration has no small-supplier threshold. Step 5: Maintain the registered and records office addresses, directors information, articles of unlimited liability, and CRA account details in the corporate books. A foreign parent should also file Form RC1 where a non-resident director or officer is involved and provide evidence of authority, powers of attorney, and any treaty certification required by the CRA or the BC Registrar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: For Canadian federal income tax, a BC ULC is a corporation resident in Canada and is taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act; Canada has no domestic check-the-box election allowing the ULC to be treated as a partnership. The Pass_Through_Eligible characterization is a cross-border elective overlay: under US Treasury Regulation section 301.7701-3, a wholly owned Canadian ULC is eligible to elect classification as a disregarded entity or partnership because its shareholders do not possess limited liability, subject to the applicable per-se rules and IRS guidance. The resulting hybrid entity status should be tested against Canada's hybrid mismatch and anti-arbitrage provisions in the Income Tax Act, the OECD BEPS Action 2 framework, and the relevant Canada-US tax treaty positions. Other statutory elections available in Canada include rollover and amalgamation elections under Income Tax Act sections 85, 87, and 88, and the annual corporate inform return and GIFI/T106 filing elections where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.eligible_tax_classification_note: For BC provincial corporate income tax, the ULC is also treated as a corporation and is subject to the BC Income Tax Act; it is not eligible for a domestic pass-through classification in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST); BC is a non-harmonized province and imposes no provincial HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.standard_rate_breakdown: Federal GST at 5.0% plus BC PST at 7.0%, for a combined BC headline consumption tax rate of 12.0% before exemptions and zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies over a trailing four-quarter period for federal GST/HST registration under the small-supplier rules; BC PST requires registration before any taxable retail sale or taxable lease in British Columbia because there is no small-supplier exemption. Passive dividend income received by a pure equity holding SPV does not constitute taxable supply for GST/HST threshold purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, CRA API-based invoice clearance, or digital stamping. A GST/HST registrant must issue prescribed invoices containing the required supplier and recipient details and retain electronic records for at least six years; EDI, XML, and PDF invoices are acceptable if complete and readable. For exported goods, the exporter must file electronic export declarations through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) using Form B13A and retain the accompanying proof-of-export file. BC PST does not require a separate real-time fiscal clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For GST/HST purposes, a BC ULC may zero-rate a supply of goods if the goods are exported from Canada in commercial quantities and documented in accordance with Excise Tax Act sections 21 and 23 and CRA GST/HST Memorandum 4-4.2. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated under Excise Tax Act sections 7 to 9 where the service is supplied to a non-resident person, is not in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, and is for consumption wholly outside Canada. Management, treasury, shareholder-loan, and dividend-receiving services may qualify only if actually supplied for consideration and all statutory tests are satisfied. Pure dividends, share transfers, and capital gains from passive equity holdings are not consideration for a supply and are outside the scope of GST/HST; they are not zero-rated because they are not taxable supplies. BC PST does not apply to goods sold for delivery outside British Columbia where the seller ships or delivers the goods directly outside the province and retains documentary proof of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Form B13A / CBSA CAED electronic export declaration for goods; for services, a signed contract evidencing an offshore supply to a non-resident recipient
Commercial Invoice with complete description of goods or services, destination, Incoterms, quantity, and value
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or other transport documentation showing the goods were physically delivered outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103/MT202 advice, or bank statement proving receipt of foreign currency payment from the non-resident purchaser
Export permit, licence, or CBSA movement record where applicable for controlled goods
CRA zero-rating evidence file containing purchase orders, correspondence, and, if claimed, Form GST11 or an applicable GST/HST ruling
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audit-sensitive. The CRA may reassess within four years of the original assessment, and without time limits in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or waiver, and may disallow zero-rating where the proof-of-export documentation is not contemporaneous or is incomplete. Disallowed supplies become taxable at 5% GST and may attract BC PST and interest where applicable; CRA may claw back refunds and input tax credits. Part IX of the Excise Tax Act imposes failure-to-register, failure-to-report, failure-to-remit, false-statement, and gross negligence penalties, together with compound daily interest; intentional evasion may lead to criminal prosecution by the CRA or CBSA and substantial fines. The 180-day repatriation benchmark is commonly incorporated in Canadian bank and exporter compliance files for proof of foreign receipt, although it is not a standalone general federal statutory deadline for all exporters. A pure equity holding SPV should document the actual cross-border flow and the non-resident recipient status carefully before claiming any zero-rating and should confirm that dividend and shareholding activity remains outside the GST/HST supply framework.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential banking supervision delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/CFT enforcement by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no separate exchange-control bureau; residual statutory authority sits with the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act (RSC 1985, c C-52), Bank of Canada Act (RSC 1985, c B-2), Bank Act (SC 1991, c 46), and Investment Canada Act (RSC 1985, c 28, 1st Supp).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility. Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and imposes no exchange-control licensing, repatriation consents, or surrender premiums on current-account or capital-account transactions. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely in a fully deliverable onshore market. Profit remittance is fiscally taxed, not exchange-controlled: 25% statutory non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (RSC 1985, c 1, 5th Supp), reducible to 0-15% under the Canada-US Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the Fifth Protocol), provided the US shareholder is the beneficial owner and the ULC is not a hybrid-mismatch structure under ITA sections 18.4-18.6. A pure-equity holding SPV must maintain paid-up-capital purity under ITA s. 89 and capital-dividend-account records; intercompany loans require transfer-pricing documentation under ITA s. 247. The Investment Canada Act mandates a post-closing Form A notification to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) whenever a non-Canadian acquires control of the ULC; a pre-closing net-benefit review applies to transactions exceeding the 2025 WTO-investor enterprise-value threshold of approximately CAD 1.325 billion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation deadlines under the Currency Act, Bank of Canada Act, or Bank Act. For a pure-equity holding SPV, receipts are investment/dividend flows rather than trade proceeds. The sole compliance overlay is FINTRAC reporting: every electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more in one transaction must be reported by the bank via an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) or Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR), and any suspicious pattern triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (SC 2000, c 17).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual-currency CAD & USD concentration)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (CAD & USD; US cross-border corridor via TD Bank NA)
Capital Escrow / Operational Account (CAD & USD; US corridor via BMO Harris Bank NA)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW-MEDIUM as primary treasury host; MEDIUM as auxiliary collection rail. FINTRAC-registered money services businesses and offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Stripe Treasury, Payoneer) cannot provide statutory deposit insurance, commercial letters of credit, CAD/USD nost account concentration, or overnight liquidity lines required by an equity-holding SPV. Using an unlicensed offshore EMI as the main clearing rail would violate Bank Act s. 539 (deposit-taking prohibition) and trigger enhanced FINTRAC scrutiny. Any payout from the ULC to an EMI account is a reportable cross-border EFT under PCMLTFA s. 7; accordingly, the EMI layer is legally viable only for low-value dividend pass-through and must be subordinated to the OSFI-regulated Tier-1 banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate for in-person attendance: OSFI Guideline B-8 and the 2020 EDD framework permit fully remote onboarding for Canadian-registered entities where at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) completes a live video identity verification with the bank's compliance officer. For a BC ULC with non-resident directors, Canadian Tier-1 banks commonly require: (i) notarized Certificate of Incumbency and director identification; (ii) certified copies of the BC Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, and Registered Office filing; (iii) a corporate-service provider agreement evidencing a real physical address; (iv) UBO questionnaire and source-of-wealth statement; and (v) original credit/registry searches. An in-person visit to a BC branch is discretionary but will be requested where the account is classified Medium-Risk-Enhanced, where the UBO cannot be electronically verified, or where the unlimited-liability attribute triggers additional committee review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited-liability designation and elective US pass-through (check-the-box under Form 8832) flagged as a hybrid-mismatch or aggressive tax-planning indicator by the bank's financial-crime model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) written SPV purpose memorandum (passive intermediate holding of Canadian/US operating subsidiaries, intercompany financing, future IPO or monetization); (ii) senior international-tax-legal opinion addressing ITA ss. 18.4-18.6 and the Canada-US treaty position on the pass-through election; (iii) executed organization chart with ownership percentages; (iv) CRA corporate returns (T2 and Part XIII remittances if any); (v) acquisition/subscription agreements evidencing commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office at a corporate-services provider with zero employees, triggering the FINTRAC letter-box entity red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) BC Registry Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles; (ii) executed corporate-services agreement with the BC law/accounting firm including fee invoices; (iii) board resolution delegating treasury authority to the account signatories; (iv) notice that the ULC is a special-purpose vehicle with no physical staff; (v) a dedicated bank-account address in British Columbia used for treasury correspondence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single inbound capital injection (e.g., CAD 15 million to CAD 50 million) from the foreign parent flagged as a surge transaction without supporting documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) executed equity subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement with arms'-length interest and maturity date; (ii) source-of-funds evidence comprising the parent entity's audited financial statements and the incoming SWIFT GPI tracker; (iii) ISED Form A notification receipt where the transaction establishes control of the ULC; (iv) the bank's Large Transaction Source-of-Funds certification signed by the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend outpayment to a non-resident shareholder at treaty-reduced withholding with no Part XIII evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) Canada-US treaty residence certificate of the shareholder (e.g., IRS Form 6166 or CRA NR301/NR302); (ii) legal memorandum confirming 5% withholding where the US parent holds at least 10% voting control and the absence of hybrid-mismatch taint; (iii) CRA Part XIII withholding remittance receipts from prior quarters; (iv) the bank's withholding instruction letter reflecting the statutory 25% fallback; (v) executed dividend declaration with paid-up-capital confirmation under ITA s. 89.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC statutory shareholder-liability risk: the bank requires net-worth covenants because unpaid liabilities of the ULC can attach to its members if ordinary creditors pursue the shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) the ULC's articles and unanimous-shareholder agreement declaring fully paid equity and a paid-up-capital certificate; (ii) a solvency opinion demonstrating net worth above the bank's threshold on both balance-sheet and cash-flow bases; (iii) a dividend-waterfall restriction tested under BC Business Corporations Act s. 68; (iv) the latest audited comparative balance sheet and intercompany loan schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) the foreign parent sends a SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the ULC's CAD/USD concentration account at its Vancouver-based Tier-1 bank (e.g., RBC, Swift ROYCCAT2VCR; TD, Swift TDOMCATTTOR/TDCCUS33; BMO, Swift BOFMCAM2); (ii) the payment purpose code must identify an equity subscription or intercompany loan, with the reference field carrying the executed agreement number and the BC corporate registry number; (iii) the bank files the FINTRAC EFTR automatically for any inbound EFT of CAD 10,000 or more; (iv) USD-wire proceeds clear via CHIPS or Fedwire correspondent networks and should be paired with a separate spot or forward FX trade to manage CAD exposure; (v) a pre-closing ISED Form A notification is required if the injection brings the non-Canadian parent to majority control; (vi) all agreements must be pre-positioned with the bank's AML team to avoid hold on source-of-funds verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a pure-equity SPV, outbound flows comprise: (i) shareholder dividends — SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer with board resolution, Part XIII withholding evidence, and ISO 20022 purpose code DIVIDEND; USD legs clear via Fedwire/CHIPS, CAD legs via Payments Canada Lynx RTGS above CAD 250,000; (ii) intercompany loan advances — MT103 with purpose code LOAN, supported by the executed loan agreement and arms'-length interest accrual; (iii) subsidiary capital calls — wire or commercial letter of credit (MT700 issuance) where the ULC acts as guarantor for an operating subsidiary, plus standby LC (MT760) for credit enhancement; (iv) all USD-funded disbursements breach the bank's US correspondent edge (RBC Bank Atlanta, TD Bank NA Wilmington, or BMO Harris Chicago) and are cleared under the receiving beneficiary's Fedwire/CHIPS routing. Every outbound remittance must be tagged with ISO 20022 structured remittance information and conform to Bank Act s. 539 if any derivative overlay is used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and outright forwards (tenors up to 24 months) under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; CAD is fully convertible onshore, so NDFs are non-standard and unnecessary for CAD/USD exposure.
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps (CCS) on matched notional to hedge intercompany loan principal and interest, executed with OSFI-regulated counterparties under full ISDA/CSA credit support.
Plain-vanilla CAD/USD vanilla options, zero-cost collars, and participations; permitted without Bank of Canada approval because Canada has no exchange-control licensing regime.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to third-currency portfolio exposures (e.g., a Latin-American or emerging-market subsidiary position) where the underlying currency lacks onshore deliverability; requires separate ISDA/CEMA documentation and board-approved counterparty limits.

Interest-rate swaps linked to floating-rate intercompany debt to stabilize net treasury cost; permissible under Bank Act s. 539 with OSFI-regulated dealer counterparties and subject to CFTC Part 43 trade-reporting thresholds if the US dealer is counterparty.
Prohibited instruments for the SPV treasury book: total return swaps and equity swaps on the ULC's own shares (dealer-board approval required and generally disfavored for passive holding entities).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each anniversary of incorporation or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The prescribed fee remains payable. Failure to file annual reports for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution or strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is generally 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each complete month late, up to 12 months, with additional interest and penalties where applicable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A British Columbia private company, including a ULC, generally has no mandatory independent audit solely because of its size or holding-company status. An audit may be required by the articles, shareholder agreement, shareholder resolution, financing terms, court order, or applicable securities-law status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) ordinarily applies to a privately held ULC. IFRS applies where the corporation is publicly accountable or elects or is otherwise required to use IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is generally no annual UBO filing with the British Columbia Corporate Registry. The corporation must maintain a transparency register identifying significant individuals at its records office, conduct an annual internal confirmation of ownership and control information, and update the register within 30 days after becoming aware of a change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Significant Individuals or Transparency Register
Articles, Certificate of Incorporation, and Corporate Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,500-8,000 for a dormant or low-complexity holding ULC; higher fees apply for material subsidiaries, cross-border tax issues, or consolidated reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate rate (Federal 15% + British Columbia provincial 12%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Intercorporate dividends received from taxable Canadian corporations are fully deductible under ITA s. 112, producing a 0% effective Part I tax rate on pure equity dividend income at the SPV level; dividends out of a foreign affiliate's exempt surplus are deductible under ITA s. 113. The federal General Rate Reduction (s. 123.4) reduces the federal rate from 38% to 15% after the 10% provincial abatement for non-CCPCs and for CCPC taxable income not eligible for the Small Business Deduction. The Small Business Deduction is not available for passive investment income of a pure-equity holding SPV, and aggregate investment income of a CCPC may attract a refundable additional tax, but a non-resident-owned ULC will ordinarily be a non-CCPC without refundable Part I tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Non-capital losses are carried back 3 years and forward 20 years (ITA s. 111(1)(a)); net capital losses are carried forward indefinitely but only against taxable capital gains (ITA s. 111(1)(b)). For a non-CCPC ULC, the carryforward horizon applies as prescribed; a hybrid-mismatch ULC should ensure losses are not inadvertently trapped or denied under GAAR.
